source.title: SLIM: Sparse Latent Steering for Interpretable and Property-Directed LLM-Based Molecular Editing
source.authors: Ming-Xu Zhang; Yu-Han Li; Lujundong Li; Da-Zhong Shen; Hui Xiong; Ying Sun

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies SAE feature extraction and steering to molecular-editing LLMs, a new setting, and reports evidence about whether sparse features can be recovered and interpreted there. It does not reproduce or test the toy-model geometry in the original source.
record.gate_note: The paper cites superposition and SAEs as motivation, but does not test feature overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, capacity competition, or dimensionality of features. Main editing-success results are not rows because they measure editing performance, not the representation claims. Table 7 feature associations and the reported single-feature steering outcomes do bear on V4.
record.test_reason: The paper builds a task-oriented SAE and steering method for molecular-editing LLMs, citing superposition only as motivation. It reports its own method's performance and feature case studies, not how often or how strongly models show superposition, neuron spreading, or SAE-recoverable sparse features. It measures no overlap, capacity or geometry.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors conclude that the task-oriented SAE gives sparse, property-aligned, interpretable features that enable training-free steering. They draw no conclusions about superposition itself.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses a task-oriented SAE with property gates and gradient alignment, then steers molecular-editing LLMs; it does not use or reproduce the original toy-network method.
record.method_sensitivity: Intervention layer and steering strength are tuned per model and property. The authors state that strength and layer require per-property and per-model tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: A supervised, gradient-aligned SAE on molecular-editing LLM activations yields features correlated with molecular properties (|rho| up to 0.93). Single-feature steering shifts the corresponding properties.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Property-supervised SAE features in chemistry LLMs can be interpretable and steerable.

record.problems: Feature interpretability measurements in Table 7 are reported for DrugAssist at Layer 3, with no uncertainty estimates. The paper does not test feature completeness, stability, canonical status, or superposition geometry. Its evaluation uses computable molecular-property oracles and has not been validated on experimental assay endpoints.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were left out. Main benchmark editing-success tables and multi-property steering results were not extracted because their metrics assess editing outcomes rather than the representation claims.

untested.parts: Capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity.

Whether LLM features are spread across many neurons, and whether an unsupervised SAE recovers sparse features. The paper only shows that a supervised, property-aligned SAE gives features correlated with oracle properties.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features. The vanilla vs task-oriented SAE ablation (cosine near zero between directions) bears on non-canonicity but is not framed or recorded as such.
Whether features are one-dimensional or multi-dimensional.

missing.what: Vanilla-SAE vs task-oriented-SAE ablation finding: steering directions have cosine similarity near zero (<0.05 DrugAssist, <0.12 Mistral). This suggests the SAE basis depends on training objective, which bears on V5 canonicity, but the paper does not frame it that way.

record.verdict_notes: The paper cites superposition only in related work. Because the SAE is trained with supervised and contrastive losses and features are selected by gate and correlation, Table 7 does not show that sparse features are naturally recoverable. The record's V4 'supports' label should be dropped, and the study treated as not testing the claim (T4).

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network storage geometry, overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from limited capacity or important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
The reported feature-interpretability table is for DrugAssist at Layer 3; the paper does not establish feature distribution across neurons in other model layers or broadly across LLMs.
Completeness, stability, and canonical status of SAE features as the model's units.
Whether the model's represented features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.
